questions.q: Before designing an extension, what does this lesson say must already be true?
options: You must have access to a multi-GPU cluster
The reproduction from the previous lesson must already be solid and trusted
The original paper's authors must approve the extension idea
You must have already written the final report
questions.explain: An extension is measured against the reproduced baseline. If the baseline isn't trustworthy yet, the comparison has no solid reference point and the extension answers nothing.

questions.q: A student's extension plan ablates one training component, switches to a new dataset, and swaps the optimizer, all in the same run. What is the main problem with this plan?
options: It will take exactly the same time as changing only one factor
Changing multiple factors at once makes it impossible to tell which change caused the observed effect
Hydra configs cannot represent more than one change
There is no problem; more changes always produce a better capstone
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly warns against combining more than one extension shape in a single run, because the result can no longer be attributed to any single cause.

questions.q: Why does the suggested extension config inherit the reproduction's settings via Hydra's defaults list rather than redefining them from scratch?
options: Hydra requires all configs to be identical
It keeps the comparison clean: everything matches the reproduced baseline except the one factor under test
It makes the sweep run faster on the GPU
It avoids the need for an experiment tracker
questions.explain: Inheriting the exact reproduced settings and changing only the ablated component isolates the effect of that one change from any other difference.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend only a handful of seeds (e.g. three) for the extension sweep rather than a large grid search?
options: Because a few seeds are enough to separate a real effect from run-to-run noise on a small benchmark, within a capstone's realistic compute and time budget
Because Weights and Biases cannot log more than three runs
Because more seeds would always show a larger effect
Because the original paper used exactly three seeds
questions.explain: A small number of seeds is a deliberate, honest scoping choice -- enough to distinguish signal from noise, not enough to claim strong statistical certainty, which the write-up should state plainly.

questions.q: The ablation shows that removing the component makes almost no difference to the result. According to this lesson, what does that mean for the capstone?
options: The capstone has failed and must be redone with a different paper
It is still a successful outcome, because a well-designed experiment that finds no effect is still informative
The result must be hidden from the final write-up
It proves the original paper's experiments were conducted incorrectly
questions.explain: A flat or negative result from a well-scoped extension is a real, useful finding, consistent with Chapter 7's point that a well-designed experiment disproving something has value.
